thread:
incident-bot: Pager: SEV-2 — GeoDNS anomaly detected for EU regions: spike in NXDOMAIN and timeouts from third-party resolvers starting ~2026-03-15T09:02Z :rotating_light:

alice.sre: I'm seeing the same from our synthetic probes across eu-west-1 and eu-central-1. NXDOMAIN and SERVFAIL up ~11-13%. Route53 answers fine from our authoritative view.

ben-net: Traceroutes look ok, but packet retransmits to a subset of our edge resolvers in eu-west. Could be upstream resolver caching or filtering.

carol-eng: Multiple customer alerts in support queue — search indexing and shard fetches failing with 502/504. Need to triage customer impact.

devon-oncall: I'm oncall and paged. Starting incident checklist. First mitigations: throttle internal probe QPS, evaluate GeoDNS policy flip to fallback pool, notify stakeholders.

alice.sre: Negative caching (NXDOMAIN) won't clear until TTL expires, but GeoDNS redirect to fallback pool might reduce queries hitting problem resolvers. We should coordinate routing change and public status copy.

ben-net: Preparing GeoDNS policy change to prefer eu_fallback pool for EU. Dry-run looks OK. Will apply and post change-id.

incident-bot: Change requested: geodns:update prefer-fallback pool=eu_fallback requested-by=ben-net

ben-net: Applied (aws change-id: C9X3Y7PAEXAMPLE). Control plane accepted; propagation to DNS control plane ~30s. External resolvers may still serve cached negatives.

alice.sre: Running external digs: ``dig @1.1.1.1 service.redwood.ai A +short`` — results are mixed (old, new, fallback). Some CF resolvers still return NXDOMAIN.

carol-eng: Draft status page: "We are investigating DNS resolution issues affecting parts of Europe. Mitigations underway." PR: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/5081234567-draft

devon-oncall: Support — collect list of high-impact customers in EU and mark urgent tickets for follow-up.

support-bot: Flagged 9 high-priority EU tickets in last 8 minutes; top affected: acme-ml, dataflow-inc, searchly.

Cloudflare-agent: We see increased SERVFAIL/REFUSED in our resolver layer for your NS delegation; investigating whether internal cache purge/backlog or upstream filtering. Preliminary note: negative cache may persist until upstream TTLs expire.

ben-net: Route53 config unchanged. Capturing tcpdump on edge resolver: ``tcpdump -i eth0 port 53 and host 1.1.1.1 -w /tmp/dns-eu-probe.pcap`` — capturing anomalies including EDNS0 size differences and some UDP truncations.

devon-oncall: If Cloudflare is rate-limiting, we might need to reduce query fanout and avoid further amplifying. Alice, pause nonessential probes.

alice.sre: Pausing probe flood. Probe QPS from our side is normal; amplification appears from client retries. Throttling probes now.

ben-net: Noted some EU ISPs respond with different EDNS0 buffer advertised size, causing truncation -> TCP fallback -> timeouts. Pushing authoritative edge config to advertise smaller UDP bufsize. Change id: edgecfg-3382.

alice.sre: After geo fallback + UDP bufsize changes, aggregate NXDOMAIN/timeout dropped: 12% -> ~2.5% over 20 minutes for eu-west. Still a few resolver clusters with 10-15% failures.

carol-eng: Status updated: "Mitigations deployed; partial recovery observed. Monitoring and engaging external provider." Published 09:34 UTC.

incident-bot: Added incident ticket INC-2026-315. Timeline auto-logged.

ben-net: Cloudflare response: backlog of negative cache purges; expected global convergence 45-90 mins depending on upstream TTLs. Case CF-2026-889 opened.

devon-oncall: Current plan: 1) keep geo fallback, 2) keep UDP bufsize tweak, 3) monitor customer errors, 4) if >5% error persists after provider convergence window, consider IP-level manual failover for top customers. Product/Legal approval required for targeted overrides.

carol-eng: Product confirmed emergency approval for targeted overrides for enterprise customers via DM. We'll only do this for top 5 contracts if needed.

alice.sre: Probe summary snapshot:
```
09:02 UTC - NXDOMAIN eu probes: 11.8%
09:18 UTC - After geodns fallback: 3.4%
09:28 UTC - After UDP bufsize adjust: 2.1%
```

support-bot: Ticket update: 27 active, 7 escalated to SEs. Support sending retry/backoff guidance to affected customers.

devon-oncall: I'll hold this incident until provider confirms purge or error rate <1% for 30m. Next handoff target 10:30 UTC. If we see regression, escalate immediately.

ben-net: Documented actions in runbook: geodns flip (C9X3Y7PAEXAMPLE), edge UDP bufsize (edgecfg-3382), probe throttle, CF engagement CF-2026-889.

Cloudflare-agent: Update: background purge progress ~55%. We'll continue monitoring.

alice.sre: Real-user error rate for EU services down ~65% from peak. Some customers still impacted due to negative caching.

carol-eng: Posting customer impact summary to PMs and GTM: peak degraded request rate ~15-25% for EU, mitigations reduced visible failures significantly. Draft sent.

devon-oncall: Good work team. I'll file a short postmortem stub to incidents tracker and assign RCA owners (net/infra/product) once CF confirms resolution.

incident-bot: Incident state: mitigation in progress -> partial customer impact. Next update in 30m or on change.

status-bot: Public status updated: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/5081234567 — "Partial degradation in EU due to DNS resolver anomalies; mitigations deployed."

carol-eng: Support will continue one-on-one outreach. I'll keep draft RCA notes here.

devon-oncall: Holding until convergence confirmed. Hand-off plan stands. If external provider confirms full purge, we'll transition to recovery and start RCA scheduling.

incident-bot: Thread suspended. Reopen on alerts or manual reopen.
